answer: Bind each agent's payout key to a National Park Service Commercial Use Authorization, the permit any outfitter needs to lead trips through a canyon or across a glacier. A CUA names one operator, requires liability insurance and an annual fee, and rangers spot-check permits at trailheads amid the umber rock. A sybil farm of 1,000 fake agents would need 1,000 insured operators at roughly $1,500 each in fees and premiums, about $1.5M a year before earning a single reward.
